summary: Preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated 727 KB payload at install time
details: @servicetitan/marketing-email-components@20.2.4 declares a preinstall hook that runs setup.mjs, which downloads the Bun runtime from GitHub releases into a temp directory (os.tmpdir()/bun-dl-*), extracts it via system 'unzip' or PowerShell 'Expand-Archive', chmods the binary to 0755, and then execFileSyncs the Bun binary against a bundled sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a single-line ~727 KB '// @bun @bun-cjs' blob with a shuffled string/opcode array, a rotation routine (WV8StW), and a character-decoder (hc1jfK9) that reconstructs identifiers at runtime — heavy obfuscation that blocks static inspection of the payload's network destinations and side effects. The package advertises itself as React email template components; there is no legitimate reason for such a package to fetch an alternate language runtime at install time and use it to execute an opaque 727 KB script. The alternate-runtime pattern (Bun instead of Node) also evades Node-based install-time scanners that only trace Node-resolved code. The download-extract-chmod-execute chain runs automatically on npm install with the installer's privileges, giving whoever authored the payload arbitrary code execution on every installing machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
